title: Ways to Climb With One or Two Steps
statement: Count ways to reach step n when each move advances one or two steps. The order of moves matters, so 1+2 and 2+1 are different ways. Print it modulo 1000000007. The base cases are one way to stand at step zero and one way to reach step one. Compute each later value from the previous two values.
reference_python:
import sys
n=int(sys.stdin.read());m=1000000007;a,b=1,1
for _ in range(n):a,b=b,(a+b)%m
print(a)

title: Minimum Coins for an Amount
statement: Given coin denominations and a target amount, find the minimum number of coins needed to form exactly that amount. Each denomination can be used any number of times. If the amount cannot be formed, print -1. Coins are positive integers, and the target may be zero, which requires zero coins. Use one-dimensional dynamic programming over amounts, considering every denomination for each state.

print(-1 if dp[t]>t else dp[t])

title: Number of Ordered Sum Combinations
statement: Given distinct positive integers and a target, count the ordered sequences of numbers that sum to the target. Reusing a number is allowed, and sequences with the same values in different orders count separately. Print the answer modulo 1000000007. The empty sequence is the single way to make target zero. Let dp[x] count sequences summing to x, and append each available number as the final element of a sequence for a smaller sum.

title: Maximum Sum Without Adjacent Elements
statement: Choose a subset of the array with no two chosen positions adjacent, maximizing the sum. You may choose no elements, so the answer is never negative. Values may be negative or positive. At each position, either skip it and retain the best answer through the previous position, or take it and add its value to the best answer two positions earlier. Track these two states while scanning left to right.

title: Longest Common Subsequence Length
statement: Given two strings, find the length of their longest common subsequence. A subsequence preserves character order but need not be contiguous. Characters are lowercase English letters. Use dynamic programming: matching final characters extend the best subsequence of the two prefixes by one; otherwise discard one final character and take the better result. Only the previous and current rows are needed.
input_format: two lowercase strings on separate lines
reference_python:
import sys
a,b=sys.stdin.read().split();dp=[0]*(len(b)+1)
for x in a:
 prev=0
 for j,y in enumerate(b,1):old=dp[j];dp[j]=prev+1 if x==y else max(dp[j],dp[j-1]);prev=old
print(dp[-1])

title: Edit Distance
statement: Find the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and substitutions needed to transform string A into string B. Each operation costs one, and characters are lowercase English letters. If the final characters match, no operation is needed for that pair; otherwise consider inserting, deleting, or replacing one character. Use a rolling-row dynamic program to compute the answer without storing the full table.
reference_python:
import sys
a,b=sys.stdin.read().split();dp=list(range(len(b)+1))
for i,x in enumerate(a,1):
 nd=[i]+[0]*len(b)
 for j,y in enumerate(b,1):nd[j]=dp[j-1] if x==y else 1+min(dp[j],nd[j-1],dp[j-1])
 dp=nd
print(dp[-1])

title: Count Paths in a Grid With Obstacles
statement: A grid has open cells marked '.' and blocked cells marked '#'. Starting at the top-left cell, count paths to the bottom-right cell using only moves right or down. If either endpoint is blocked, the answer is zero. Print the count modulo 1000000007. The grid is rectangular and every row has the same width. A one-row DP array is enough because each cell depends on the cell above and the cell to its left.
input_format: r c followed by r grid rows
reference_python:
import sys
z=sys.stdin.read().split();r,c=map(int,z[:2]);g=z[2:];m=1000000007;dp=[0]*c;dp[0]=1
for i in range(r):
 for j in range(c):
  if g[i][j]=='#':dp[j]=0
  elif j:dp[j]=(dp[j]+dp[j-1])%m
print(dp[-1])

statement: Determine whether the array can be split into two groups with equal total sum. Every element must belong to exactly one group, and the groups need not be contiguous. If the total sum is odd, equality is impossible. Otherwise determine whether some subset sums to half the total. Use one-dimensional subset-sum DP updated in descending order so each value is used at most once.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. Selected elements must retain their original order but may have gaps. Equal values cannot both extend a strictly increasing subsequence. Use a list of minimal tail values: for each number, replace the first tail greater than or equal to it, or append it if it is larger than all tails. The length of this list is the answer.
reference_python:
import sys,bisect
a=list(map(int,sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()))[1:];tails=[]
for x in a:
 i=bisect.bisect_left(tails,x)
 if i==len(tails):tails.append(x)
 else:tails[i]=x
print(len(tails))
intended_complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

title: Minimum Jumps to the End
statement: Each array element gives the maximum number of positions that can be advanced from that index. Starting at index zero, find the minimum jumps needed to reach the final index. If the last index cannot be reached, print -1. Values are nonnegative. Greedily maintain the farthest index reachable from the current jump range and count a jump whenever the current range ends. An array of length one needs zero jumps.
input_format: n followed by n nonnegative integers
reference_python:
import sys
a=list(map(int,sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()))[1:];n=len(a);jumps=end=far=0;ans=0
for i in range(n-1):
 far=max(far,i+a[i])
 if i==end:
  if far<=i:ans=-1;break
  jumps+=1;end=far
print(ans if ans==-1 else jumps)

title: Count Islands in a Grid
statement: A grid contains land cells marked '1' and water cells marked '0'. Count islands, where land cells are connected horizontally or vertically, but not diagonally. The grid may contain no land. Scan every cell; whenever an unvisited land cell is found, increase the count and flood-fill its connected component. Mark cells as visited as they are added to a queue to avoid processing them repeatedly.
input_format: r c followed by r binary strings

title: Shortest Word Transformation
statement: Given a start word, a target word, and a dictionary of equal-length words, find the minimum number of single-character changes needed to transform start into target, with every intermediate word in the dictionary. Each change must alter exactly one character. If no transformation exists, print -1. The start word need not be in the dictionary, but the target must be. Use breadth-first search over words, generating neighbors by changing each character to each lowercase letter.
input_format: start target n; n dictionary words

title: Single Number Among Triples
statement: Every integer in the array appears exactly three times except one integer that appears once. Find the unique integer. Values are signed 32-bit integers, so the answer may be negative.  if sum((x&0xffffffff)>>b&1 for x in a)%3:ans|=1<<b
print(ans-(1<<32) if ans>>31 else ans)

title: Count Divisors
statement: For each positive integer n, count its positive divisors. Divisors occur in pairs d and n/d, so it is sufficient to test candidates up to the square root. If n is a perfect square, count its square-root divisor only once. The input contains q positive integers, and each answer is printed on its own line.
input_format: q followed by q positive integers
reference_python:
import sys,math
d=list(map(int,sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()));out=[]
for n in d[1:]:
 ans=0
 for x in range(1,math.isqrt(n)+1):
  if n%x==0:ans+=1 if x*x==n else 2
 out.append(str(ans))
print('\n'.join(out))
intended_complexity: O(sqrt(n)) time per query, O(1) auxiliary space
